title: Sealed classes, and when expressions the compiler forces you to finish

videos.script: A session is planned, running, done. Then one day somebody adds skipped. How many places in the app now need to know what skipped means? {{when}} This lesson is about the compiler answering that question for you. It starts with when, Kotlin's switch, which is an expression and has no fall-through. {{enum}} Then enums: a fixed set of values. Add one, and every when without an else stops compiling, with the missing branch named. {{sealed}} Then sealed classes: a fixed set of types, each carrying its own data. A running session has a start time. A planned one does not, and cannot. {{exhaustive}} Add a fourth shape, and watch the compiler list every place that has to handle it. And watch what one careless else does to that list. {{state}} Last, the shape every Android screen uses. Loading, loaded, failed. Three states that exist, and none that do not.
